# Settings

Every setting J4n has: 207, from 16 packs. A setting of a pack that is off does nothing. *Live* no: an edit takes effect at the next start. *Shown*: under Settings › Features (else only under All). *Follows*: the value `auto` means what that other setting says. Under each table, the full text of every setting whose first sentence is not all of it.

## base

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `approval.inside` | str | `auto` | auto, on, off | yes | yes | lanes=orchestrate | The Gate says yes by itself to edits and tests that stay inside the project. |
| `box.net` | bool | `true` |  | no |  |  | Whether a boxed task may use the network. |
| `box.unavailable` | str | `refuse` | refuse, here | no |  |  | When no box can run here (a container has no user namespaces): `refuse` stops the task and says the way out; `here` runs it unboxed and says so. |
| `box.use` | str | `auto` |  | no |  |  | Which `box` row a task in the place `box` is put behind: `auto` is the first whose probe passes. |
| `brief.cli` | str | `claude` | off, claude, all | yes |  |  | Whether a doer that takes no Brief is given one anyway, as text after its goal: the sections that fit (the contract and the project card on the first line of a session; the plan line, the files this line touched, notes you kept, what earlier tasks remember, messages and the reports of branches on every line), and nothing for a section with nothing in it. |
| `brief.plain_answer` | bool | `false` |  | yes |  |  | Whether the turn that writes your answer is asked, in one sentence, to say what a thing is in words and to add a few words when it cites an id from the project. |
| `brief.project_card` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Whether the first turn of a session is given the project card in its Brief: the stable facts of the folder (its manifests, the top of its tree, its scripts, the titles of its docs), derived from the files with no model, each made again when its file changes, at most 300 tokens. |
| `brief.recall` | bool | `false` |  | yes |  |  | Whether the first turn of a task whose goal is the goal of an earlier task is shown what that task's report claimed, as the Brief section `remembered`: only claims that were checked, whose files are as they were (a claim is dropped when its file's hash changed), worded as an old report's claims and not as facts, at most 150 tokens. |
| `chats.archive.auto` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | On: a chat whose plan is done, every item shown to hold by its check or its review (none left `unproven`), is archived by itself once it has been done for half an hour, the time the list waits before it folds it. |
| `chats.archive.idle` | dur | `1d` |  | yes |  |  | How long a chat is left alone before `/archive` takes it: its turns over and ok, nothing waiting, cooling or queued, no open plan item, and no line or turn for this long. |
| `chats.archive.keep` | dur | `14d` |  | yes |  |  | How long a chat stays in the archive before it is removed: it leaves every list, the Log row `chat.removed` says what was deleted, and the doer's own session files of the chat go with it; the Log's other rows stay, it is a chain. |
| `chats.message.chars` | int | `2000` | 1–2000 | yes |  |  | The most characters of a message between chats: a longer one is cut and the row says so. |
| `chats.message.hops` | int | `3` | 1–3 | yes |  |  | How long a cause chain of messages may be: a message sent because of a message is one hop, and the one past this is held, and you are asked `hold their messages?`. |
| `chats.message.rate` | int | `6` | 1–6 | yes |  |  | How many messages one sender may send in a minute: the next is held and you are asked `hold their messages?`; nothing is dropped. |
| `chats.on` | bool | `false` |  | no | yes |  | Every line can become a chat of its own, with its own agent session. |
| `check.after` | bool | `true` |  | yes | yes |  | Run the project's own tests after a task changed files. |
| `compact.at` | num | `0.7` | 0.1–1.0 | yes |  |  | How full a doer's context may be (0 to 1) before the session is shrunk at the next boundary. |
| `compact.max` | int | `3` | 0–20 | yes |  |  | How many times one chain of tasks may have its session shrunk. |
| `complete.decider` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | A Decider puts first the suggestion you most likely mean, marked ~, after a pause in typing: it picks among what code found and writes nothing. |
| `complete.decider_day` | int | `300` |  | yes |  |  | The most times a day the Decider is asked to order the suggestions in this project. |
| `complete.on` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Tab completes what you type: a command, a chat, a command's words, a file, a name in a field. |
| `context.line.in` | int | `200` | 0–100000 | yes |  |  | The size of a typical small line, in fresh input tokens, that `/context` adds to what a session holds to say what the next line costs. |
| `context.line.out` | int | `150` | 0–100000 | yes |  |  | The size of the answer to a typical small line, in output tokens, for the same sum. |
| `cool.max` | dur | `6h` |  | yes |  |  | The longest a task is let wait out a limit; a limit that ends later stops the task, and it can be carried on from the menu. |
| `cost.calibrate.size` | int | `3000` | 100–30000 | yes |  |  | How many whole numbers `:calibrate yes` has the doer write: the size of the request that makes a pair for a plan's window. |
| `cost.plan.min_n` | int | `5` | 1–100 | yes |  |  | How many pairs of a window's movement and the list cost spent in it a plan's window needs before its plan cost is measured and not assumed. |
| `cost.plan.on` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Whether J4n reads the limit windows a provider shows and says what a request cost the plan, next to its list cost. |
| `cost.show` | str | `both` | plan, list, both | yes | yes |  | The money shown for a request on a plan: its share of the plan, the list price, or both. |
| `doer.keys` | str | (empty) |  | no |  |  | The agent programs given the API key J4n keeps for their provider (typed in Agents › Providers) in place of their own sign-in, as connector ids with spaces between (`claude codex`). |
| `doer.scope` | str | `project` | project, user | no |  |  | What a CLI doer (claude) is started with besides the project: `project` (the default) gives it the project's own settings and the Gate, and leaves out the operator's user settings and enabled plugins, their MCP servers (the account's connectors included), the Claude in Chrome browser, and the tools that reach other sessions or the account (`ListAgents`, `SendMessage`, `PushNotification`, `RemoteTrigger`, `DesignSync`); `user` starts it as the tool loads itself. |
| `flow.map_width` | int | `4` | 1–16 | yes |  |  | How many items of a flow's `map` step run at once, each a task of its own (a claude process, each). |
| `keys.hold` | str | `auto` | auto, off | no |  |  | Holding ⌥ shows each tab's number beside it, where the terminal can say a key is held: `auto` asks it to report every key, so a held ⌥ is seen, and the numbers stay until ⌥ is let go; `off` asks for less, and the numbers show for a moment after each ⌥1–9 instead. |
| `keys.pass` | str | `GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN` |  | no |  |  | The key variables of the environment J4n was started in that every agent program is given as they are, beside those its own row names, with spaces between (`GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN`). |
| `lane.account` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The account the doer `lane.doer` runs as, one of its accounts (empty: its own sign-in). |
| `lane.doer` | str | (empty) |  | yes | yes |  | The agent a new chat starts with (empty: J4n picks one that works). |
| `lane.model` | str | (empty) |  | yes | yes |  | The model of that agent (empty: the agent's own default). |
| `lanes` | str | `single` | single, auto, wide, orchestrate | yes | yes |  | How much J4n does by itself: single, auto, wide or orchestrate. |
| `librarian.more` | int | `3` | 0–100 | yes |  |  | The most a task may ask the librarian for with `context`: past it the tool says so and the task works with what it has. |
| `librarian.on` | bool | `false` |  | no |  |  | On: a task's context is made for that task and that doer: code picks what a model's Brief holds (the project card is held back from a short line and from a plain question that names no file), the skills are the ones that fit, and where two fit equally and there is room for one, Jev chooses at the ask point `librarian`. |
| `look.chart` | str | `dither` | dither, plain | yes |  |  | How the charts are drawn: `dither` is half-block pixels with a dithered body under each line and in each bar, where the terminal has truecolor and colour is on; `plain` is braille dots and block bars. |
| `look.gauge` | str | `auto` | auto, line, slice | yes |  |  | How a meter is drawn, by the width it has: `auto` is one slice of a circle and its number in the composer, a chat's row and any strip short of width, the thin line (at most 8 cells) where a page has room, and a long bar only on the page about that number (Usage); `line` is the thin line (`━━──── 41%`) and `slice` is the circle slice wherever a context is shown. |
| `look.generate` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | The look's pass: what the look file does not cover (a kind, a number's field, a page's key) is counted, and once in a while the ask point `look` (jev first) is asked for entries for those only, checked before use. |
| `look.keys_row` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | The keys row, the last row of the screen: the keys of the page that is open, a few words each. |
| `look.misses` | int | `12` | 1–10000 | yes |  |  | How many misses start a pass (else a day with any); never more than one pass an hour, never while a task works. |
| `look.time` | str | `ago` | ago, clock | yes |  |  | How a row says when it happened: `ago` is how long ago, from the screen's own clock, and it moves on by itself (`now`, `5s`, `3m`, `2h1m`, `1d3h`); `clock` is the time of day (`13:43`). |
| `loop.followups` | int | `3` | 0–20 | yes |  |  | How many times in a row a task that ended with work left is carried on by itself, in its own session. |
| `need.waived` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The needs of a feature that you chose to go on without, by id (`orchestrate`). |
| `offload.prices` | str | `haiku=1 sonnet=3 opus=5 fable=8 nano=1 mini=1 flash=1 lite=1 pro=3` |  | yes |  |  | What each model costs per token, relative to the others, as `word=number` pairs: the first word that a model's name holds, as a whole word, gives its price (`claude-sonnet-5-5` holds `sonnet`; `gemini` does not hold `mini`). |
| `orchestrate.access` | str | `auto` | auto, on, off | yes |  | lanes=orchestrate | `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. |
| `orchestrate.ask` | str | `writes` | writes, always, never | yes |  |  | Which chats wait for your yes before they start: `writes` (the default) the ones that write, `always` every one, `never` none, so a split starts at once. |
| `orchestrate.catalogue` | int | `1500` | 200–20000 | yes |  |  | The most tokens the list of J4n's features, doers and skills that the quick look is shown may take (about four characters each). |
| `orchestrate.chat_top` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The dearest model a chat of a split is briefed on, as a model word (`sonnet`): a brief whose model costs more by `offload.prices` runs on this word instead, and the chat says so. |
| `orchestrate.chats` | int | `3` | 1–4 | yes |  |  | The most chats one line may start when the quick look says it splits (3 by default, never more than 4). |
| `orchestrate.digest` | int | `400` | 50–5000 | yes |  |  | The most tokens the digest of one chat may take: what it came to (done, sent back, blocked), what it cost, the claims of its report as the checks found them, the files, the checks it ran, how sure it was and what it left open. |
| `orchestrate.digests` | int | `3` | 0–20 | yes |  |  | How many of the newest digests Main's next turn is shown (3 by default), with a line for each chat it started. |
| `orchestrate.held` | str | `main` | main, operator | yes |  |  | Who decides on a chat's part that was stopped (blocked, its work held in its worktree). |
| `orchestrate.look` | str | `auto` | auto, on, off | yes |  | lanes=orchestrate | `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. |
| `orchestrate.look_doer` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The doer that makes the quick look (empty: the cheap tier's, `plan.cheap_doer`). |
| `orchestrate.look_model` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The model of the quick look, as a model word of its doer (`haiku` is the newest Haiku; empty: the cheap tier's, `plan.cheap_model`). |
| `orchestrate.read_big` | int | `200000` | 0–1000000000 | yes |  |  | How many bytes of files a line may name before reading them is worth a chat of its own: a split whose chats only read stays one lane unless the paths the line names hold more than this (200 kB by default). |
| `orchestrate.read_model` | str | `kind` |  | yes |  |  | The questions of the read that the quick model may answer, as names with spaces between: `kind` (what the line is, and the parts of a split), `goes_on` (whether it goes on from the last answer), `chat` (which open chat it is about), `asked` (which doer it asks for). |
| `orchestrate.review` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | On (the default): under `orchestrate`, when Main works a line itself and changes files, another doer reads the change with a clean context and names its concerns; they go back to Main, at most three rounds (`plan.sends`), and what is left after that is yours to decide. |
| `orchestrate.way` | str | `ask` | ask, decide | yes |  |  | When the read of a line is unsure of the way of working (it said split and named no parts): `ask` (the default) shows one choice before any work starts, one lane or split into chats, with the read's way recommended and a row for your own words; `decide` takes the read's way, one lane, with no question. |
| `orchestrate.writers` | int | `2` | 0–4 | yes |  |  | How many chats that write may work at once (2 by default); a brief past it is worked by Main itself. |
| `packs.full` | bool | `false` |  | no | yes |  | Load every pack built in (J4n full) in place of J4n basic. |
| `pick.hand` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The ask points you pick at yourself, by id (`chats look`): at each of their asks one pick row shows the options numbered, the suggested one first. |
| `plan.cheap_doer` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The doer the cheap branches run on, scouts and pieces, over the election (empty: the cheapest model of a doer that is signed in, the thread's own doer first, when `offload.prices` prices one of its models; else elected, or the thread's). |
| `plan.cheap_model` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The model the cheap branches (scouts and pieces) run on, as a model word of their doer: the newest match is taken (`haiku` is the newest Haiku), and one that matches none refuses the branch (empty: the cheapest model of the doer, by `offload.prices`; a tier never picks Opus or Fable). |
| `plan.doer` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The doer that makes the plan and its replans, when it is not the thread's own (empty: the thread's). |
| `plan.grow` | int | `3` | 0–50 | yes |  |  | How many items a replan may add before the operator is asked (`:plan accept`, `:plan reject`). |
| `plan.lay_refused` | str | `block` | block, retry | yes |  |  | When a checked and reviewed piece cannot be laid in, because the folder holds other changes to a file it changed: `block` (the default) blocks it at once, with its work kept where it is and named, and the main lane or you decide on it; its doer works in a copy of the project that does not hold the folder's changes, so a retry cannot clear them. |
| `plan.model` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The model that makes the plan and its replans, as a model word of the planning doer (`opus`, `opus 5`): the newest match is taken, and one that matches none refuses the planning turn. |
| `plan.review_doer` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The doer a review branch runs on, over the election (empty: elected, and never the one that wrote the work). |
| `plan.review_model` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The model a review branch runs on, as a model word of its doer (empty: the thread's own, or the elected one). |
| `plan.revisions` | int | `3` | 0–20 | yes |  |  | How often a plan's approach is revised before the operator is asked: the next revision asks and stops. |
| `plan.sends` | int | `3` | 0–20 | yes |  |  | How many times an item of a plan is sent back before it is blocked: the next one is the block. |
| `plan.usd_line` | num | `0.5` | 0–1000 | yes |  |  | What the branches of one line may take together, in dollars; past it no new branch starts (the running ones go on to their own caps). |
| `probe.wait` | num | `30` | 0–600 | yes |  |  | With no operator there (`j4n run`, piped mode, `--approval deny` or `full`), how many seconds a line waits for the probe cases of the deciders and models in the chain of the point it asks, when they have not been proved yet (a fresh home): the cases are put now, on a thread of their own, and the line goes on when they are written or the time is gone. |
| `profile` | str | `full` | full, auto, lean | no |  |  | What a CLI doer is started with: `full` (every task as the tool would load it by itself: all its tools, MCP servers, skills and memory; the default), `auto` (a task whose role the connector's row names in `profile.lean_for`, a chore or a decider, is started lean, the rest full), `lean` (every task lean: `Read` is its only tool and no MCP server, skill or memory file is loaded, much less to read on a first turn). |
| `rabbit.reads` | int | `30` | 3–1000 | yes |  |  | How many places a task may read without changing anything before it is asked to say what it has found. |
| `read.big_heads` | bool | `false` |  | yes |  |  | Draw a level-1 heading larger with kitty's text sizing (kitty 0.40 and later only; other terminals ignore it). |
| `read.fold_code` | int | `12` | 0–1000 | yes |  |  | A fenced code block longer than this many lines is folded after them in `calm` (0 never folds). |
| `read.links` | str | `osc8` | osc8, plain | yes |  |  | What a link is: `osc8` makes the words open their address on a click in a terminal that takes it (kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm, iTerm2, foot, Alacritty); `plain` says the address in words after them. |
| `read.style` | str | `calm` | calm, full | yes |  |  | How prose is drawn: `calm` leaves a blank row between paragraphs, before headings and folds long code; `full` is denser, with no extra blank rows and code not folded. |
| `read.terms` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Whether an id of the project's docs in an answer (`ADR-12`, `BUG-7`, `UX3`) is drawn with a few faint words saying what it is, the first time it is named. |
| `read.width` | int | `76` | 30–200 | yes |  |  | Where prose wraps, in columns (a narrower screen wraps sooner). |
| `retry.auto` | bool | `false` |  | yes |  |  | Whether a turn that failed with what may mend (a dropped connection, not a limit and not a refusal) is put to the ask point `retry`: the same doer again, another doer, or a stop. |
| `retry.max` | int | `1` | 0–5 | yes |  |  | How many failures in a row end with a try again or a hand to another doer; the failed turn is not counted, so 1 is two tries at most. |
| `route.cooling` | int | `3` | 1–100 | yes |  |  | How many limits or server errors within five minutes make a host cooling: it is not offered, and a thread bound to it follows `route.failover`. |
| `route.failover` | str | `wait` | wait, move, ask | yes |  |  | What a bound thread does when its host is cooling after a burst of limits: `wait` (the task is waited out like any limit), `move` (to the next host, with a notice of what the cold cache costs) or `ask` (say so, and let the operator move it). |
| `route.floor_gap` | num | `0.2` | 0–1 | yes |  |  | How far under the best host's pass rate for a role a host must fall to be no longer offered for it (0.2 is twenty points). |
| `route.hosts` | bool | `false` |  | yes |  |  | Whether J4n elects a host for a model when a thread binds, among the hosts a `model` row lists. |
| `route.lambda` | num | `-1` | -1–100 | yes |  |  | What a minute of waiting is worth, in dollars, when a host is picked. |
| `route.lambda_base` | num | `0.003` | 0.000001–100 | yes |  |  | A minute of waiting when nobody waits and nothing hangs on the result, in dollars. |
| `route.lambda_blocked` | num | `2` | 1–1000 | yes |  |  | How many times more a minute is worth when a flow waits on the result. |
| `route.lambda_tight` | num | `2` | 1–1000 | yes |  |  | How many times more a minute is worth when a deadline is near. |
| `route.lambda_waiting` | num | `3` | 1–1000 | yes |  |  | How many times more a minute is worth when the operator is on the lane (a line typed in the last five minutes). |
| `route.min_n` | int | `5` | 1–1000 | yes |  |  | How many tasks of a role a host must have run for its record to count. |
| `route.quant` | str | `any` |  | yes |  |  | A precision a host may not sell the model at, as `no-fp4`, `no-int4` (several: `no-fp4,no-int4`); `any` allows all. |
| `route.uptime_floor` | num | `95` | 0–100 | yes |  |  | Hosts whose listed uptime, in percent, is below this are not offered. |
| `session.big` | int | `40000` | 0–100000000 | yes |  |  | How many tokens a session holds before `session.mode auto` may end it: a session at or under this is resumed even when it is cold, since writing a small one to the cache again costs less than the carry-over's start. |
| `session.mode` | str | `auto` | resume, auto, each | yes |  |  | When a line carries on in the doer's session: `resume` always (a session is for ever), `auto` (a line starts a new session when carrying on would be cold, the provider's cache having lapsed, and the session holds more than `session.big` tokens; a provider whose cache life is not said is never cold), `each` (every line you type starts its own session). |
| `setup.card` | bool | `true` |  | no |  |  | Whether a start shows the Setup card while no agent works or the Decider is not set up. |
| `stuck.fails` | int | `4` | 2–100 | yes |  |  | How many commands in a row may fail before a task is asked to step back. |
| `tabs.all` | bool | `false` |  | yes | yes |  | Show every tab and page, the ones that have nothing to show yet too. |
| `theme.corners` | str | `round` | round, square | yes |  |  | The corners of a box: `round` or `square`. |
| `theme.density` | str | `normal` | compact, normal, roomy | yes |  |  | How much room a row takes: `compact`, `normal` or `roomy`. |
| `theme.fill` | str | `match` | match, terminal, paint | yes |  |  | What paints the background: `match` sets the terminal's own background to the palette's while J4n runs (so its padding is the same colour) and gives it back on the way out, `terminal` paints none, `paint` paints every cell. |
| `theme.frame` | str | `round` | pipes, gutter, hang, round, airy | yes |  |  | How the trees and the chat are drawn: `round` (a tree of pipes with rounded corners, the default), `pipes` (the same tree with square corners), `airy` (no lines, a dot and an arrow), `gutter` (one word a row in a column) or `hang` (a lane with no tree, its steps hung from a rail). |
| `theme.marks` | str | `auto` | auto, icons, unicode, ascii, words | yes | yes |  | What the marks are drawn with: icons, plain symbols, ASCII or words. |
| `theme.motion` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Whether the name of a doer that works breathes, and whether the track under a line that is being taken (sent, routed, a chat opened, a doer started) draws its line to the next mark. |
| `theme.mouse` | str | `on` | on, off | yes |  |  | Whether the wheel (and the touchpad) scrolls the chat and the pages: `on` asks the terminal to report the mouse, so ⇧-drag selects text (the terminal's own selection needs ⇧ held); `off` leaves the mouse to the terminal, which may turn the wheel into ↑↓. |
| `theme.palette` | str | `jjj` | jjj, dusk, paper, ember, mono, contrast | yes | yes |  | The colours of the screen. |
| `theme.title_place` | str | `inside` | inside, border, none | yes |  |  | Where the title of a box goes: `inside`, `border` or `none`. |
| `theme.you` | str | `bracket` | bracket, band, mark | yes |  |  | How the operator's own line is drawn in the chat: `bracket` is the words plain between two caps in the accent colour, the head of the tree under it; `band` is the words on a raised band across the width with the time at its right and no icon; `mark` has no band and no icon on the pipes or the hang: the words start at the left edge in your colour, closer to the border than the rows under them. |
| `trust.max_wrong` | num | `0.25` | 0–1 | yes |  |  | The share of an answerer's labelled answers for an ask point that may be wrong. |
| `trust.min_n` | int | `20` | 1–200 | yes |  |  | How many labelled answers an answerer needs for an ask point before its wrong share counts. |
| `wall.warn.at` | num | `0.88` | 0.0–0.99 | yes |  |  | How much of a task's time (0 to 1) may pass before its doer is told the time is nearly up and to write its files now; 0 tells it nothing. |
| `wall.warn.min` | dur | `2m` |  | yes |  |  | The shortest time given to a task that its doer is told about before the end; a shorter one is a probe or a test. |
| `watch.canary` | bool | `false` |  | yes |  |  | Whether a new release of a tool that touches or breaks what J4n uses is run once, as the source's `canary` row says, in a folder of its own, and its shape compared with a good run's. |
| `watch.cold_min` | int | `1440` | 5–43200 | yes |  |  | Minutes between two looks at the sources of the cold tier. |
| `watch.digest` | str | `weekly` | weekly, daily, open, never | yes |  |  | When the releases that touch what J4n uses are said together as one line (the Updates tab under Grow always lists them): `weekly`, `daily`, `open` (once each time J4n starts) or `never`. |
| `watch.hot_min` | int | `30` | 5–1440 | yes |  |  | Minutes between two looks at the sources of the hot tier (a tool a running task drives). |
| `watch.issues` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Whether the issues a `gh-rest` source tracks (a workaround, a bug J4n filed) are asked for; each is one request of GitHub's REST, under the same floor as a gap in a feed. |
| `watch.upstream` | bool | `false` |  | yes |  |  | Whether J4n asks, quietly and on a timer while it runs, whether the tools it uses have a new release: one conditional request per source, a 304 writes nothing, and only a change reaches the Log. |
| `watch.warm_min` | int | `240` | 5–10080 | yes |  |  | Minutes between two looks at the sources of the warm tier. |
| `web.local` | bool | `false` |  | no |  |  | Whether a fetch may reach the machine J4n runs on and the network around it (loopback, 10.x, 192.168.x, a link-local address such as the cloud's metadata service). |
| `web.search` | str | (empty) |  | no |  |  | The id of the connector that answers a search of `web`: one with the dialect `http-json`, whose first argument is the query (a SearXNG, a Brave key, any endpoint). |
| `weigh.answer` | str | `light` |  | yes |  |  | The doer that answers a line weighed as `answer`: a chat model with no tools (the pack `jev` has one, `light`). |
| `weigh.on` | bool | `false` |  | no |  |  | On: before a line is sent it is weighed, and the weight chooses where it goes: `answer` (a greeting, thanks, a general question: a cheap model with no tools and no project answers it, the doer `weigh.answer`), `light` (a short question about the project: a lean session on the cheap tier, `plan.cheap_doer` and `plan.cheap_model`, when its doer has a lean profile) or `task` (the doer of the chat, as always). |
| `work.apply` | str | `auto` | auto, off | yes |  |  | What happens to the change of a task that worked in a worktree when it is over: `auto` lays it into your folder at once if it applies cleanly and touches nothing you changed there but an empty file git does not track, where the task made that file; `off` keeps the worktree until it is taken. |

- **`approval.inside`**: `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. On: an approval no rule has a say about (or that only the rule for an unreadable line asks, for invisible characters inside the text a here-document gives Python) is said yes to by the Gate when its effect stays inside the project, a chat's worktree or the task's own temporary folder: an edit, a test run (`cargo test`, `uv run pytest`, `npm test`), a linter, a script of the project named for a check (`scripts/verify.sh`), a remove of build folders, Python on the line that opens only files it names inside the project. A line that is inside but for the paths of some Python, built while it runs, is put to a Decider (the point `inside`), which may say `inside` or `ask`; no Decider, or an unsure one, asks you. You are still asked for anything outside the project, the network, credentials, a delete that is not of build folders, `git push`, a deploy and a remote line, and for what a rule of yours asks. The Log says who said yes: `rule:gate` ("inside the project: …") or `decider:<id>` ("inside, harmless: …"). A run that denies every ask keeps it off.
- **`box.net`**: Whether a boxed task may use the network. The agents are API clients: leave it on unless the row can cut it and the work needs none.
- **`brief.cli`**: Whether a doer that takes no Brief is given one anyway, as text after its goal: the sections that fit (the contract and the project card on the first line of a session; the plan line, the files this line touched, notes you kept, what earlier tasks remember, messages and the reports of branches on every line), and nothing for a section with nothing in it. `claude` (the default): the doers that read a folder of skills as their own, which is claude; `all`: every doer that takes no Brief (codex, gemini, opencode, pi); `off`: none. The skills it picks are not in it: claude has them as its own folder, another doer after its goal.
- **`brief.plain_answer`**: Whether the turn that writes your answer is asked, in one sentence, to say what a thing is in words and to add a few words when it cites an id from the project. A model doer gets the sentence in its Brief's contract; a doer that runs a program of its own gets it after its text through the wrapper that carries the kit card. Planning turns and branches never get it; nothing about formatting is ever sent. Off until it is shown not to lower the pass rate.
- **`brief.project_card`**: Whether the first turn of a session is given the project card in its Brief: the stable facts of the folder (its manifests, the top of its tree, its scripts, the titles of its docs), derived from the files with no model, each made again when its file changes, at most 300 tokens. On by default.
- **`brief.recall`**: Whether the first turn of a task whose goal is the goal of an earlier task is shown what that task's report claimed, as the Brief section `remembered`: only claims that were checked, whose files are as they were (a claim is dropped when its file's hash changed), worded as an old report's claims and not as facts, at most 150 tokens. Off until it is measured.
- **`chats.archive.auto`**: On: a chat whose plan is done, every item shown to hold by its check or its review (none left `unproven`), is archived by itself once it has been done for half an hour, the time the list waits before it folds it. A chat with no plan has no such proof and is archived by `/archive` only. Off: only you archive.
- **`chats.archive.idle`**: How long a chat is left alone before `/archive` takes it: its turns over and ok, nothing waiting, cooling or queued, no open plan item, and no line or turn for this long. A day: a chat you come back to the next morning is not taken, and the list still folds it from sight after half an hour.
- **`chats.archive.keep`**: How long a chat stays in the archive before it is removed: it leaves every list, the Log row `chat.removed` says what was deleted, and the doer's own session files of the chat go with it; the Log's other rows stay, it is a chain. Two weeks is long enough to find an answer again and short enough that the session files do not pile up. `0s` keeps the archive for ever.
- **`chats.message.chars`**: The most characters of a message between chats: a longer one is cut and the row says so. It may be set lower, never above the core's own floor of 2,000.
- **`chats.message.hops`**: How long a cause chain of messages may be: a message sent because of a message is one hop, and the one past this is held, and you are asked `hold their messages?`. Never above the core's floor of 3.
- **`chats.message.rate`**: How many messages one sender may send in a minute: the next is held and you are asked `hold their messages?`; nothing is dropped. Never above the core's floor of 6.
- **`chats.on`**: On: every prompt can be a chat of its own: a chat is a thread with its own doer session (`c3`), a plan's branch is a chat under it (`c3.1`), and the first screen is the orchestrator, which has no doer and shows a pinned list of the chats and the rows of what it did with your lines. A line typed there goes to the chat it matches (a file it names, a subject it shares) and opens a new chat only when it matches none; Jev (the ask point `chats`) is asked only when code has no match, and you are asked only when more than one chat matches or the one that does is cooling or failed. `:new`, `:fresh`, `:clear`, `:chats`, `:top` act on chats, `⏎` goes into one, `esc` goes up. Off until it has been used: with it off the screen and the core are what they were, nothing is probed, asked or written. Read at the start.
- **`check.after`**: Whether the project's own check (kind `check`) is run after a task that changed files, where it worked. On by default: the project's tests run unasked and may take long, so turn it off here when they do.
- **`complete.decider`**: A Decider puts first the suggestion you most likely mean, marked ~, after a pause in typing: it picks among what code found and writes nothing. It acts only where a Decider is set up and has passed its cases, at most complete.decider_day times a day; off, or with none, code's order alone.
- **`complete.decider_day`**: The most times a day the Decider is asked to order the suggestions in this project. Past it, code's order alone until the next day, said once in the chat.
- **`complete.on`**: Tab completes what you type: a command, a chat, a command's words, a file, a name in a field. The rest of the best one stands dim after the cursor; ⇥ takes it and steps on, ⇧⇥ steps back, → takes it, ⌃→ one word, esc puts back what was typed. Off, ⇥ only takes a question's recommended option.
- **`cost.calibrate.size`**: How many whole numbers `:calibrate yes` has the doer write: the size of the request that makes a pair for a plan's window. Raise it when the announced list cost is more than one request of this size takes; the announcement says what a request has to cost, and the Log says what it did.
- **`cost.plan.min_n`**: How many pairs of a window's movement and the list cost spent in it a plan's window needs before its plan cost is measured and not assumed. Fewer pairs: the plan cost is the over-estimate the plan's `assume` says, marked `assumed`.
- **`cost.plan.on`**: Whether J4n reads the limit windows a provider shows and says what a request cost the plan, next to its list cost. Off: no window is read or written, `run.metrics` carries the list cost alone, and a cap is in list cost. On: the plan cost is measured or assumed (`cost.plan.min_n`), and a cap is in plan cost.
- **`cost.show`**: Which money the status bar, the chat and the Usage tab say for a request that ran on a plan: `plan` (what it took of the plan), `list` (what it costs at list price) or `both` (the plan cost first, the list cost beside it). A request on no plan has one number.
- **`doer.keys`**: The agent programs given the API key J4n keeps for their provider (typed in Agents › Providers) in place of their own sign-in, as connector ids with spaces between (`claude codex`). A program named here gets that key in its environment when it is started (`kept:` in its row's `secrets`), never in its arguments, and J4n refuses to start it while no key is kept; a task that runs as an account keeps the account's sign-in. A program not named here is started with its own sign-in, and a key typed for its provider reaches only J4n's own HTTP doers. Empty by default. Read at the start.
- **`doer.scope`**: What a CLI doer (claude) is started with besides the project: `project` (the default) gives it the project's own settings and the Gate, and leaves out the operator's user settings and enabled plugins, their MCP servers (the account's connectors included), the Claude in Chrome browser, and the tools that reach other sessions or the account (`ListAgents`, `SendMessage`, `PushNotification`, `RemoteTrigger`, `DesignSync`); `user` starts it as the tool loads itself. The project's `.mcp.json` is not passed (a project nobody trusted could name a program to run): servers are connectors, pinned and put to the Gate. Read at the start; a session begun before the change is carried on in a new child.
- **`flow.map_width`**: How many items of a flow's `map` step run at once, each a task of its own (a claude process, each). The default is four; a machine with little memory says less.
- **`keys.pass`**: The key variables of the environment J4n was started in that every agent program is given as they are, beside those its own row names, with spaces between (`GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN`). A variable whose name ends in _KEY, _TOKEN, _SECRET or _PASSWORD reaches no program J4n starts unless its row or this list names it; a tool, a shell line of J4n's own agent, the Python kernel and an MCP server are never given one from this list. The default keeps the GitHub sign-in that an agent's own `gh` and `git` read. Read at the start.
- **`lane.account`**: The account the doer `lane.doer` runs as, one of its accounts (empty: its own sign-in). Agents › Setup sets it with the doer: ⏎ on `claude · claude-1`.
- **`lane.doer`**: The doer a thread that is not bound yet is bound to, when it is ready (empty: the election chooses). `:setup doer codex` sets it.
- **`lanes`**: What acts on its own: `single` (a line is a task; no plan keeper, no branches), `auto` (the plan keeper is on; branches by rule are scouts and reviewers, and the main lane is the only writer), `wide` (also pieces, written in held worktrees and merged one at a time) or `orchestrate` (the one switch of the mode: Main is a chat with a doer session of its own and works each line itself; while it is the word the quick look at each plain line can open chats, and the crew's seats, the envoys, the plan keeper and the messenger are on, each by its own setting `orchestrate.look`, `crew.on` and `crew.envoys`, which are `auto` and follow the word unless you set them yourself; turning the word on or off starts Main's session fresh). `:lanes auto` says it while J4n runs.
- **`librarian.on`**: On: a task's context is made for that task and that doer: code picks what a model's Brief holds (the project card is held back from a short line and from a plain question that names no file), the skills are the ones that fit, and where two fit equally and there is room for one, Jev chooses at the ask point `librarian`. What is held back is named to the doer, which asks for it with the tool `context` (a CLI doer through `j4n.call('context', …)` in the kit), and each addition is a `brief.added` event with its reason. Off by default: with it off the Brief is what it was, byte for byte, nothing is probed, nothing is asked and `context` is offered to nobody. Read at the start.
- **`look.chart`**: How the charts are drawn: `dither` is half-block pixels with a dithered body under each line and in each bar, where the terminal has truecolor and colour is on; `plain` is braille dots and block bars. Under `dither`, a terminal without truecolor, colour off or the ascii marks still draw `plain`.
- **`look.gauge`**: How a meter is drawn, by the width it has: `auto` is one slice of a circle and its number in the composer, a chat's row and any strip short of width, the thin line (at most 8 cells) where a page has room, and a long bar only on the page about that number (Usage); `line` is the thin line (`━━──── 41%`) and `slice` is the circle slice wherever a context is shown. All count what is used.
- **`look.generate`**: The look's pass: what the look file does not cover (a kind, a number's field, a page's key) is counted, and once in a while the ask point `look` (jev first) is asked for entries for those only, checked before use. Off: the built-in look and what you set on Settings › Look.
- **`look.keys_row`**: The keys row, the last row of the screen: the keys of the page that is open, a few words each. Off, the row goes back to the page.
- **`need.waived`**: The needs of a feature that you chose to go on without, by id (`orchestrate`). A feature whose need is waived does not pick a model by itself, and its card is not shown again; a need that is not in the list is asked about once while the feature is on and lacks it.
- **`offload.prices`**: What each model costs per token, relative to the others, as `word=number` pairs: the first word that a model's name holds, as a whole word, gives its price (`claude-sonnet-5-5` holds `sonnet`; `gemini` does not hold `mini`). They are the shape of the providers' list prices, yours to correct. A tier is found by them: `cheap` is the lowest price, `standard` the next one up, and Opus and Fable are never picked by a tier, only by a pin. A model no word matches has no tier. Offload reads them too.
- **`orchestrate.access`**: `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. On: each chat of a split that writes is given read-only copies, in its own worktree and at the paths they have in the project, of the files of another chat that its brief reads (as that chat has them now) and of the folder's build files and the files Main's line wrote there; each copy is kept as its source is, and the chat is told when one changes. A chat asks for more with the tool `access`: the plan answers first, then the Deciders, then Main (`access <id>: yes` or `no`); the guard refuses secrets, keys, a doer's own state, paths outside the project and in `.git` whatever was said. A copy is never the chat's work: it is not laid into your folder, and J4n makes no commit in your project. Off: each chat sees the project as last committed and its own files, and tests against stand-ins.
- **`orchestrate.ask`**: Which chats wait for your yes before they start: `writes` (the default) the ones that write, `always` every one, `never` none, so a split starts at once. The card shows each brief, its doer, its model and what it may spend.
- **`orchestrate.catalogue`**: The most tokens the list of J4n's features, doers and skills that the quick look is shown may take (about four characters each). A list over it is shortened: commands first, then the packs' summaries, then the skills.
- **`orchestrate.chat_top`**: The dearest model a chat of a split is briefed on, as a model word (`sonnet`): a brief whose model costs more by `offload.prices` runs on this word instead, and the chat says so. Empty (the default): Main's brief names the model, as it planned.
- **`orchestrate.chats`**: The most chats one line may start when the quick look says it splits (3 by default, never more than 4). The briefs past it are worked by Main itself.
- **`orchestrate.digest`**: The most tokens the digest of one chat may take: what it came to (done, sent back, blocked), what it cost, the claims of its report as the checks found them, the files, the checks it ran, how sure it was and what it left open. Never its transcript.
- **`orchestrate.digests`**: How many of the newest digests Main's next turn is shown (3 by default), with a line for each chat it started. Older ones stay in the Log, so what Main holds does not grow with the chats it starts.
- **`orchestrate.held`**: Who decides on a chat's part that was stopped (blocked, its work held in its worktree). `main` (the default): under `--approval full`, where every yes is given, Main is asked and its answer acts: a line `held c1: lay` lays the part's held work in this folder once more, checked after, and `held c1: drop` leaves it where it is held; a line in another form leaves it held, and each part is decided once. Without `--approval full` the part waits for you either way. `operator`: Main is told of it, and laying it in is always yours.
- **`orchestrate.look`**: `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. On: a plain line is first read, once: the Deciders answer what they are sure of (what the line is, whether it goes on from the last answer, which open chat it is about, which doer it asks for), a cheap model with no tools is asked only what they left open, and where nothing settles a question the line goes to Main as typed; the read is written to the Log and Main's row says what the line was taken as, by whom, and why a question stayed open. When it says split, Main's own model (read-only) writes a brief for each part and J4n opens a chat for each brief that passes its checks (a chat that writes waits for your yes, as `orchestrate.ask` says); a part that is not opened stays with Main, and the Log says why. Commands, `@c3` and `@claude` (a doer named in exact syntax, with its model after it), and a line typed while a task works are not read, and the Log says why for the last. Off: the line goes to Main as typed.
- **`orchestrate.look_doer`**: The doer that makes the quick look (empty: the cheap tier's, `plan.cheap_doer`). It reads only: it is given no tool that writes.
- **`orchestrate.look_model`**: The model of the quick look, as a model word of its doer (`haiku` is the newest Haiku; empty: the cheap tier's, `plan.cheap_model`). A word that matches none refuses the look, and the line goes to Main as typed.
- **`orchestrate.read_big`**: How many bytes of files a line may name before reading them is worth a chat of its own: a split whose chats only read stays one lane unless the paths the line names hold more than this (200 kB by default). Counted by J4n from the files, never judged by the model.
- **`orchestrate.read_model`**: The questions of the read that the quick model may answer, as names with spaces between: `kind` (what the line is, and the parts of a split), `goes_on` (whether it goes on from the last answer), `chat` (which open chat it is about), `asked` (which doer it asks for). The Deciders answer any question they are sure of; for a name left out of this list the model is not asked, the question stays open and the line goes to Main as typed, which the row says. The default is `kind` alone: the model is less reliable on `goes_on`, `chat` and `asked`, so they stay with the Deciders (and `@claude` names a doer exactly); `kind` made no false split and a miss leaves the line one lane, as typed.
- **`orchestrate.review`**: On (the default): under `orchestrate`, when Main works a line itself and changes files, another doer reads the change with a clean context and names its concerns; they go back to Main, at most three rounds (`plan.sends`), and what is left after that is yours to decide. The reviewer is `plan.review_doer` and `plan.review_model`, or the election. A split's chats are reviewed either way. Off: Main's own lane is not reviewed.
- **`orchestrate.way`**: When the read of a line is unsure of the way of working (it said split and named no parts): `ask` (the default) shows one choice before any work starts, one lane or split into chats, with the read's way recommended and a row for your own words; `decide` takes the read's way, one lane, with no question. A run with nobody to ask always takes the read's way, and the Log says so.
- **`orchestrate.writers`**: How many chats that write may work at once (2 by default); a brief past it is worked by Main itself. Each writes in a worktree of its own, held until its work is checked.
- **`packs.full`**: J4n full: on, every pack built in is loaded (the empty `test` pack is left out) and J4n is whole; off, the default, J4n basic loads the gate, the guard, the way to grow J4n and the connectors of the other CLI agents, plus the packs your folder already uses, and every other pack waits on Settings › Packs. A pack you turn on or off there wins over this switch. Read at the start.
- **`pick.hand`**: The ask points you pick at yourself, by id (`chats look`): at each of their asks one pick row shows the options numbered, the suggested one first. A digit picks, Enter takes the suggested one, Esc takes the point's fallback, and a minute without a key does too. The needs card offers it where a Decider would answer and none is set up.
- **`plan.cheap_doer`**: The doer the cheap branches run on, scouts and pieces, over the election (empty: the cheapest model of a doer that is signed in, the thread's own doer first, when `offload.prices` prices one of its models; else elected, or the thread's). The checker is not one: it runs the item's check command and uses no model.
- **`plan.doer`**: The doer that makes the plan and its replans, when it is not the thread's own (empty: the thread's). Its model is `plan.model`, else the doer's default; the items keep the thread's doer and model.
- **`plan.lay_refused`**: When a checked and reviewed piece cannot be laid in, because the folder holds other changes to a file it changed: `block` (the default) blocks it at once, with its work kept where it is and named, and the main lane or you decide on it; its doer works in a copy of the project that does not hold the folder's changes, so a retry cannot clear them. `retry` sends it back to its item as a failed check is, until `plan.sends` blocks it.
- **`plan.model`**: The model that makes the plan and its replans, as a model word of the planning doer (`opus`, `opus 5`): the newest match is taken, and one that matches none refuses the planning turn. Empty: the thread's own model. The items keep the thread's model.
- **`probe.wait`**: With no operator there (`j4n run`, piped mode, `--approval deny` or `full`), how many seconds a line waits for the probe cases of the deciders and models in the chain of the point it asks, when they have not been proved yet (a fresh home): the cases are put now, on a thread of their own, and the line goes on when they are written or the time is gone. 0 is the switch off: such an answerer is skipped until a run with time has proved it. A person at the screen never waits; the cases run beside the line.
- **`profile`**: What a CLI doer is started with: `full` (every task as the tool would load it by itself: all its tools, MCP servers, skills and memory; the default), `auto` (a task whose role the connector's row names in `profile.lean_for`, a chore or a decider, is started lean, the rest full), `lean` (every task lean: `Read` is its only tool and no MCP server, skill or memory file is loaded, much less to read on a first turn). A session begins with its profile and keeps its prompt when it is resumed.
- **`read.terms`**: Whether an id of the project's docs in an answer (`ADR-12`, `BUG-7`, `UX3`) is drawn with a few faint words saying what it is, the first time it is named. The words are the first sentence of the table row in the docs that defines the id, read once and again when a doc changes; an id the docs do not define is left alone. ⏎ on the line opens the row.
- **`retry.auto`**: Whether a turn that failed with what may mend (a dropped connection, not a limit and not a refusal) is put to the ask point `retry`: the same doer again, another doer, or a stop. Off: it stops, and the menu offers `try again`.
- **`route.hosts`**: Whether J4n elects a host for a model when a thread binds, among the hosts a `model` row lists. Off: the model's default endpoint, with a session id so the gateway keeps one host and its cache. Off by default.
- **`route.lambda`**: What a minute of waiting is worth, in dollars, when a host is picked. Below zero (the default, -1), J4n works it out each time: the base below, raised when you are waiting at the keyboard, when a flow waits on the result, or when a deadline is near. A pin of 0 would pick the slowest, cheapest host, so it is a number you chose.
- **`route.lambda_base`**: A minute of waiting when nobody waits and nothing hangs on the result, in dollars. About the break-even for code generation.
- **`route.min_n`**: How many tasks of a role a host must have run for its record to count. Under it the host is unknown: it gets tasks that only read first.
- **`route.quant`**: A precision a host may not sell the model at, as `no-fp4`, `no-int4` (several: `no-fp4,no-int4`); `any` allows all. The measured floor per host and role is not built yet.
- **`session.mode`**: When a line carries on in the doer's session: `resume` always (a session is for ever), `auto` (a line starts a new session when carrying on would be cold, the provider's cache having lapsed, and the session holds more than `session.big` tokens; a provider whose cache life is not said is never cold), `each` (every line you type starts its own session). A new session is told the chat's last answers, the open plan line and the files changed, made from the Log, never the old transcript; a row in the chat says why, and `:resume` takes the old one back.
- **`setup.card`**: Whether a start shows the Setup card while no agent works or the Decider is not set up. On until the card is answered once in this J4n home: its `open Setup` turns it off for every project, and `later` asks again at the next start. Agents › Setup is there either way.
- **`tabs.all`**: Every tab and page there is. Off, the default: five tabs (Chat, Usage, Agents, Log, Settings), Tasks while `lanes` acts on its own, a pack's pages while its pack or switch is on, and a page that lists nothing is left out where nothing would be missed (Agents › Tools, Services, MCP, Trust; Providers leaves out the ones with no connector and the ones whose program is not here). On: Tasks and Decisions, Grow, Updates and TODO, Agents › Lab, Settings › Look, This Session, Loop and Gates, every provider, and the empty pages too.
- **`theme.marks`**: What the marks are drawn with: `auto`, `icons` (a Nerd Font), `unicode`, `ascii` or `words`. `auto` draws icons where the terminal draws them itself (ghostty, WezTerm, kitty) or a Nerd Font is installed, and unicode where neither is found; the row says which and why. An installed font is not proof that the terminal draws with it: if the marks show as boxes or blanks, pick `unicode`. For the icons, install a Nerd Font, choose it as the terminal's font, then pick `icons` or `auto`.
- **`theme.motion`**: Whether the name of a doer that works breathes, and whether the track under a line that is being taken (sent, routed, a chat opened, a doer started) draws its line to the next mark. Off, they stand still.
- **`trust.max_wrong`**: The share of an answerer's labelled answers for an ask point that may be wrong. Over it, with `trust.min_n` labels, the answerer is skipped for that point until the operator trusts it again.
- **`wall.warn.at`**: How much of a task's time (0 to 1) may pass before its doer is told the time is nearly up and to write its files now; 0 tells it nothing. Only a doer that takes words while it works is told.
- **`watch.canary`**: Whether a new release of a tool that touches or breaks what J4n uses is run once, as the source's `canary` row says, in a folder of its own, and its shape compared with a good run's. Off: no install and no run.
- **`watch.digest`**: When the releases that touch what J4n uses are said together as one line (the Updates tab under Grow always lists them): `weekly`, `daily`, `open` (once each time J4n starts) or `never`. What breaks something is said at once whatever this is.
- **`watch.issues`**: Whether the issues a `gh-rest` source tracks (a workaround, a bug J4n filed) are asked for; each is one request of GitHub's REST, under the same floor as a gap in a feed. Off: none is asked.
- **`watch.upstream`**: Whether J4n asks, quietly and on a timer while it runs, whether the tools it uses have a new release: one conditional request per source, a 304 writes nothing, and only a change reaches the Log. Off (the default): no request leaves, and Grow › Updates `r` says so. Turn it on in Settings › All › watch.upstream.
- **`web.local`**: Whether a fetch may reach the machine J4n runs on and the network around it (loopback, 10.x, 192.168.x, a link-local address such as the cloud's metadata service). Off: only the public internet is fetched.
- **`web.search`**: The id of the connector that answers a search of `web`: one with the dialect `http-json`, whose first argument is the query (a SearXNG, a Brave key, any endpoint). Left empty, the tool says how to connect one.
- **`weigh.answer`**: The doer that answers a line weighed as `answer`: a chat model with no tools (the pack `jev` has one, `light`). Not ready (no key, not installed): the line is a task, and the Log says why.
- **`weigh.on`**: On: before a line is sent it is weighed, and the weight chooses where it goes: `answer` (a greeting, thanks, a general question: a cheap model with no tools and no project answers it, the doer `weigh.answer`), `light` (a short question about the project: a lean session on the cheap tier, `plan.cheap_doer` and `plan.cheap_model`, when its doer has a lean profile) or `task` (the doer of the chat, as always). The weight never changes the model of the chat's own session. The local table of wordings (`phrase` rows with a `weight`) is tried first, then Jev, and a line is a task when Jev is not there or has not passed its cases; each row in the chat says what the line was taken as, and `:ask <line>` sends it to the chat's doer as it is. Off by default: with it off nothing is weighed and nothing is written. Read at the start.
- **`work.apply`**: What happens to the change of a task that worked in a worktree when it is over: `auto` lays it into your folder at once if it applies cleanly and touches nothing you changed there but an empty file git does not track, where the task made that file; `off` keeps the worktree until it is taken. A change that cannot be laid down is always kept, with the reason.

## connect

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connect.auto` | bool | `false` |  | no |  |  | Whether `/connect` connects a program with no question about connecting: `off` (the default) asks at `connect:is` and shows a Proposal; `on` tries the program in the box, takes the best guess of the rows where it would ask, and adds a connector whose canary passed, saying so. |
| `connect.relearn` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Whether a connected program that changes what it says is learned again: when a run of it says nothing J4n can read, the Connect flow is run for it in the box. |

- **`connect.auto`**: Whether `/connect` connects a program with no question about connecting: `off` (the default) asks at `connect:is` and shows a Proposal; `on` tries the program in the box, takes the best guess of the rows where it would ask, and adds a connector whose canary passed, saying so. It changes no guard: the box, the read mode, the Gate and the asks for a wider trust stand as they are.
- **`connect.relearn`**: Whether a connected program that changes what it says is learned again: when a run of it says nothing J4n can read, the Connect flow is run for it in the box. `on` (the default) swaps its row where `connect.auto` is on, and proposes the new row where it is off; `off` leaves the row as it is and the Agents tab says `drifted`.

## contribute

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contribute.mode` | str | `ask` | ask, auto, off | yes |  |  | Whether this J4n notices what is wrong with J4n and keeps it on this machine: `ask` (the default) and `auto` find, and anything that would be public asks (in this version nothing is sent at all); `off` finds nothing. |


## crew

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crew.chat_settings` | str | `model effort tools.allow tools.deny personality` |  | yes |  |  | The settings a chat may hold of its own, as words with a space between: `model`, `effort`, `tools.allow`, `tools.deny` and `personality` act on the chat's turns. |
| `crew.checkers` | int | `2` | 1–4 | yes |  |  | Under `crew.goal = quality`: how many reviews of a plan may run at once (2 by default); a review that has no place waits for one to end. |
| `crew.envoys` | str | `auto` | auto, on, off | yes |  | lanes=orchestrate | `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. |
| `crew.goal` | str | `cost` | cost, quality | yes |  |  | What the crew works for: `cost` (the default) leaves everything as it is; `quality` aims at a steady outcome nearest to what was asked. |
| `crew.links` | str | `star` | star, declared | yes |  |  | Who may talk to whom, while the crew is on. |
| `crew.on` | str | `auto` | auto, on, off | yes |  | lanes=orchestrate | `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. |
| `crew.record_min` | int | `5` | 1–50 | yes |  |  | Under `crew.goal = quality`: how many results of a doer for a role make its own record count (5 by default); with fewer, the public board's score for that doer stands in for it, if the seeds have one. |
| `crew.voice_max` | int | `1200` | 200–4000 | yes |  |  | The most characters a seat's own words may hold (1200 by default). |

- **`crew.chat_settings`**: The settings a chat may hold of its own, as words with a space between: `model`, `effort`, `tools.allow`, `tools.deny` and `personality` act on the chat's turns. A setting that is machine-wide, about money, or about safety is refused whatever is listed here, and so is one a chat does not act on yet.
- **`crew.checkers`**: Under `crew.goal = quality`: how many reviews of a plan may run at once (2 by default); a review that has no place waits for one to end. They are counted apart from `orchestrate.chats`.
- **`crew.envoys`**: `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. On, with `crew.on` and `lanes` set to `orchestrate`: the operator may open an envoy (the command `envoy`), a chat that interviews them, drafts a charter that they sign in its chat, and sends Main their request while the charter holds. Every question of the work shows in the envoy's chat. An envoy acts only under a charter you signed in its chat. Needs a screen: a run with no one to ask has no envoy.
- **`crew.goal`**: What the crew works for: `cost` (the default) leaves everything as it is; `quality` aims at a steady outcome nearest to what was asked. Under `quality`: a writing chat's review is made by the `reviewer` seat, a critic reads the whole change against your own words when a plan ends, `orchestrate.chats` is its hard 4 (writers stay as set), reviews at once are held to `crew.checkers`, and a doer is picked by its record (how often its work passed and how steady it was; the public board's scores while it has too little of one) and not by cost. Needs `crew.on`.
- **`crew.links`**: Who may talk to whom, while the crew is on. `star` (the default) is the routing there is: you or an envoy to Main, Main to a chat and an envoy, a chat to Main with its report and its opinion, a question of the work to its envoy. `declared` is only the `[[link]]` rows you or a pack wrote: a message no row carries is refused with the reason, a row's `hops` is the most times one thread may pass it, and a cycle of rows that no `hops` caps is left out when they load.
- **`crew.on`**: `auto` (the default): on while `lanes` is `orchestrate`, off else; `on` and `off` that you set win. On: while chats are briefed by Main, a brief may name a seat (`seat`): the seat's words and access are given to that chat, and the narrower access of the seat and the brief wins. Off: the field is not read and a chat is started as before.
- **`crew.voice_max`**: The most characters a seat's own words may hold (1200 by default). A seat with more is left out and the doctor says which.

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grow.allow_after` | int | `3` | 2–50 | yes |  |  | How many times the operator has to allow exactly the same action before J4n proposes to remember it for this project. |
| `grow.tips` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Whether J4n proposes changes to itself from what it sees (the same yes given again and again, a machine answerer's confidence). |

- **`grow.tips`**: Whether J4n proposes changes to itself from what it sees (the same yes given again and again, a machine answerer's confidence). Off: it proposes nothing; proposals already made stay.

## guard

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `guard.files` | str | `.env .env.* *.env *.pem *.key id_rsa id_ed25519 id_ecdsa credentials.json *-credentials.json service-account*.json *.tfvars .npmrc .pypirc .netrc .pgpass` |  | no |  |  | The names of the files that a task behind a box (`box`, `worktree-box`) sees only as their view, with each secret in them replaced by a placeholder: words separated by spaces, `*` for any run of characters and `?` for one, matched against the file's name wherever it is in the task's folder. |

- **`guard.files`**: The names of the files that a task behind a box (`box`, `worktree-box`) sees only as their view, with each secret in them replaced by a placeholder: words separated by spaces, `*` for any run of characters and `?` for one, matched against the file's name wherever it is in the task's folder. A file such a name picks is covered only if the redactor finds a secret in it (so `.env.example` stays as it is), and never if it is binary or over 1 MiB.

| `inbox.mode` | str | `off` | off, show, auto | yes |  |  | What happens to a line typed while a task works: `off` (the default) steers the task at once, as ever; `show` gives the line a tag and a receipt and delivers it at the task's settled boundary (steer and hold lines as the section `inbox` of the next turn, a side line as a task of its own); `auto` also steers a task at once with a `steer` line whose rule has measured precision. |

- **`inbox.mode`**: What happens to a line typed while a task works: `off` (the default) steers the task at once, as ever; `show` gives the line a tag and a receipt and delivers it at the task's settled boundary (steer and hold lines as the section `inbox` of the next turn, a side line as a task of its own); `auto` also steers a task at once with a `steer` line whose rule has measured precision. An unknown word is `off`.
- **`inbox.related`**: The share of a line's words found in the task (its goal, the paths it changed, the item in hand) at or over which the line is about the task: tag `steer`. A first guess.
- **`inbox.unrelated`**: The share at or under which the line is about something else: tag `side` when it is a question or names a path the task has not touched, else `hold`. A first guess.

## kit

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit.grants` | str | (empty) |  | no |  |  | The Python packages a task may add with `need("name")` without asking, as names with spaces between (`pandas numpy`); the operator's standing yes. |
| `kit.judge` | str | `off` | off, on | no |  |  | Whether code in the kit's kernel may send text to the decider Jev (`j4n.judge`, `choose`, `score`). |
| `kit.keep` | num | `0.15` | 0–1 | no |  |  | The line under which `j4n.keep` dismisses an item the decider judged: p below it is dropped, p at or over it is kept. |
| `kit.mode` | str | `off` | off, on | no |  |  | Give the own agent a Python kernel that keeps its variables for the task. |
| `kit.model` | str | `light` |  | no |  |  | The connector (a chat model, `is = "model"`) that `j4n.model` asks, last, on what the decider kept. |
| `kit.off` | str | (empty) |  | no |  |  | The parts of the kit that are turned off, as names with spaces between: library functions (`dedup heads`) and recipes as `recipe:<name>` (`recipe:each`). |

- **`kit.grants`**: The Python packages a task may add with `need("name")` without asking, as names with spaces between (`pandas numpy`); the operator's standing yes. Any other package asks first, once, before the cell runs (a yes for this task or session is a grant too). A Block row of the Gate wins over this. Empty by default: every install asks.
- **`kit.judge`**: Whether code in the kit's kernel may send text to the decider Jev (`j4n.judge`, `choose`, `score`). `off` (the default) sends nothing: those calls raise an error that names this setting. `on` sends the text of the items it is asked about, after the leak check: a call with a line that looks like a secret is refused, whole. Set it per project, when its text may go to Jev. Needs kit.mode on. An unknown word is `off`.
- **`kit.keep`**: The line under which `j4n.keep` dismisses an item the decider judged: p below it is dropped, p at or over it is kept. 0.15 by default, so only what the decider clearly rules out is dismissed.
- **`kit.mode`**: Whether the own agent is given the tool `py`: Python in a kernel that keeps its variables for the task (standard library only, no network where the task is in a box, one cell is one Gate call). `off` (the default) offers nothing and starts nothing; `on` offers it, and starts a kernel at the task's first cell. An unknown word is `off`.
- **`kit.model`**: The connector (a chat model, `is = "model"`) that `j4n.model` asks, last, on what the decider kept. `light` in the pack jev by default; with no key, `j4n.model` says so.
- **`kit.off`**: The parts of the kit that are turned off, as names with spaces between: library functions (`dedup heads`) and recipes as `recipe:<name>` (`recipe:each`). A cell that calls one is refused, and it is left out of `help(j4n)`, `j4n.recipes()` and the offer line; nothing is deleted, and taking the name out turns it on again. It acts from the next start (its row says `⟳`). J4n proposes a part for this list when no cell has used it over the last 100 cells in at least 5 tasks (`kit_use`); the operator's yes writes it. Empty by default: every part is on.

- **`ledger.mode`**: Whether a thread that settles is reported: `on` (the default) writes one report from the Log each time nothing of the thread is open and a task of it has ended (a chat card, and the reports under Usage); `off` says nothing new, as before. An unknown word is `off`.
- **`ledger.model`**: For `ledger.prose = mixed`: a doer, a colon and the model it is asked for (`light:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`, `light` is the small model of the pack jev). With no such doer the paragraph is dropped and says why; the facts stand.

## offload

| Setting | Type | Default | Words | Live | Shown | Follows | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offload.busy_at` | num | `0.8` | 0–1 | yes |  |  | How full a subscription's five-hour window is to be called busy (0 to 1): a chore does not start on a busy window while another is free. |
| `offload.cap_usd` | num | `2` | 0–1000 | yes |  |  | What the chores that are paid per request (a gateway key) may take in a day, in dollars (UTC). |
| `offload.max_words` | int | `30` | 4–200 | yes |  |  | The longest line that is a chore: a long line is a task, and says more than the rule can read. |
| `offload.model` | str | `haiku` |  | yes |  |  | The model of a chore on claude, as a model word of its doer (the newest match is taken). |
| `offload.on` | bool | `true` |  | yes |  |  | Send light chores (reads, searches, test runs) to a lighter agent; nothing sent away writes. |
| `offload.order` | str | `haiku pro own` |  | yes |  |  | Where a model chore goes, first that is free: `haiku` (claude, haiku, on the main lane's account), `pro` (claude, haiku, on an account whose plan is `pro`, while the main account's window is busy) and `own` (a model on the gateway key, counted against `offload.cap_usd`). |
| `offload.own_model` | str | (empty) |  | yes |  |  | The model of a chore on the gateway key, as a model word of the doer `own` (empty: the doer's own default). |
| `offload.worth` | num | `3` | 0–100 | yes |  |  | How many times dearer per token the main model must be than the chore model (`offload.model`) before a chore goes to a second claude session. |
| `offload.writes` | str | `fix change edit write add implement create remove delete update refactor rename replace rewrite commit push install migrate` |  | yes |  |  | Words that make a line the main lane's however it starts: it asks for something to be changed, not read. |

- **`offload.cap_usd`**: What the chores that are paid per request (a gateway key) may take in a day, in dollars (UTC). Use of a subscription's window does not count. Past it a chore stays with the main lane, and a row says so.
- **`offload.on`**: On: a light chore (a read, a search, a test, lint or build run, a digest of a log or a diff) goes by rule to a cheaper doer and comes back as a row under the turn, told to the main lane in its next Brief; a review of the main lane's change asks first. The main lane is the only writer: nothing offloaded writes. Off: every line is the main lane's.
- **`offload.order`**: Where a model chore goes, first that is free: `haiku` (claude, haiku, on the main lane's account), `pro` (claude, haiku, on an account whose plan is `pro`, while the main account's window is busy) and `own` (a model on the gateway key, counted against `offload.cap_usd`). Words missing from the list are never used.
- **`offload.worth`**: How many times dearer per token the main model must be than the chore model (`offload.model`) before a chore goes to a second claude session. A chore costs a session of its own, so with a main model that is not much dearer it only adds cost. Under it the chore stays with the main lane and the row says why; the gateway key (`own`) is not held to it. 0: always send. A main model with no price in `offload.prices` is sent as before.

## parts

| `parts.boundary` | str | `compact` | compact, continue, reset | yes |  |  | How the next part starts: `compact` (the default) in the same session, shrunk first when the window is past `compact.at`; `continue` in the same session, never shrunk; `reset` in a new session whose Brief says the document, the part, what the run did so far and what must be kept. |

- **`parts.mode`**: Whether `:parts` runs the parts of a document you name: `off` (the default) is as ever; `show` gates each part and waits for `:parts next` before it commits it; `auto` commits a green part and goes on by itself, at most `parts.max` a run. A red gate always stops the run and commits nothing; nothing is ever pushed. An unknown word is `off`.
